grant.title: Enhancing the Security, Privacy and Robustness of AI Models and Systems (SecureAI)
grant.type: HORIZON Innovation Actions (Indirectly managed by ECCC)
grant.deadlineModel: single-stage; lump sum; ECCC-managed cybersecurity action
grant.expectedOutcome: Robust AI models and systems capable of resisting different classes of adversarial manipulation; innovative defence mechanisms for AI models and systems against new attack families; methodologies for detecting and mitigating attacks such as data poisoning, backdoor exploitation, and misclassification; AI systems leveraging privacy-enhancing technologies that maintain data confidentiality and regulatory compliance, enabling trusted in-house AI deployments (e.g., for governments and enterprises).
grant.scope: Strengthen the resilience of AI systems and algorithms against adversarial attacks, backdoor injections, and data poisoning. Develop real-time anomaly detection, mitigation techniques, and robust federated learning, in synergy with AI transparency efforts and in compliance with the AI Act. Three pillars: (1) Develop robust AI models resistant to adversarial attacks — adversarial training, robust optimisation, defence mechanisms enhancing trustworthiness; (2) Improve detection of manipulated or poisoned training data — anomaly detection, provenance tracking, automated data validation; (3) Address 'Private AI' — federated learning, secure aggregation, computing on encrypted data, quantum-safe homomorphic encryption, secure inference in deep learning, all within trusted execution boundaries (on-premise or regulated cloud) for government and enterprise sensitive-use settings.

eligibility.minConsortiumSize: Standard HE IA minimum (3 independent legal entities from 3 different MS/AC). ECCC-managed actions typically expect strong cybersecurity-cluster credentials.
eligibility.requiredCountries: Participation restricted to legal entities established in EU Member States and Associated Countries. Entities directly or indirectly controlled by a non-eligible country (or non-eligible-country entity) shall not participate. Ukraine, as an Associated Country, is eligible.
eligibility.otherConstraints: Strategic-autonomy / security-restricted call: Ownership Control Declaration required. May involve EUCI/SEN classified background or security-sensitive results. Lump-sum funding. ECCC (European Cybersecurity Competence Centre) is the indirect granting authority — proposals are evaluated with strategic-autonomy considerations in mind.

matching.resourceFit: Laboratory of Parallel and Distributed Computing supports adversarial-training and federated-learning experiments. Azure cloud provides a regulated-cloud testbed relevant for 'trusted execution boundaries'. No on-prem HSM or quantum-safe-crypto facility documented — these would have to come from a cybersecurity-cluster partner.
matching.partnershipFit: NTNU is a strong candidate — Norway has active AI-security research and a cybersecurity ecosystem (NORCICS centre etc.). Durham and TU Bergakademie Freiberg add academic depth but not cybersecurity-cluster specialisation. ZNU would benefit from a partner from an ECCC-affiliated national cybersecurity competence centre (e.g., one of the NCCs).
matching.trackRecordFit: 3 active Horizon MSCA + 14 Erasmus+ + DAAD Ukraine Digital demonstrate research-management capability. The 'AI in logistics systems for national security' UA state-budget project is directly relevant. No prior CL3 cybersecurity project documented — this is a track-record gap when bidding against established cybersecurity-cluster coordinators.
matching.warContextRelevance: High — Ukraine has operational, non-simulated data on AI-and-system attacks in wartime conditions (disinformation models, deepfake detection, drone counter-AI, OSINT pipelines under adversarial pressure). This is a genuine differentiator for the 'real-world adversarial robustness' pillar.

verdict.recommendedRole: Partner / WP lead on adversarial robustness or federated-learning workstream, with Ukrainian operational data as the differentiator. Coordinator role not realistic without prior CL3 cybersecurity history.
strengths: Direct AI Lab core fit on at least two of the three topic pillars (adversarial robustness, federated/private AI)
Adjacent track record: 'AI in logistics systems for national security' provides credible references
Ukrainian wartime operational data on AI-under-attack is rare and valuable for evaluators
≈127 days to deadline is enough to join a forming consortium and contribute a well-scoped WP
risks: ECCC-managed cybersecurity calls are competitive — strong cybersecurity-cluster credentials are usually expected, which ZNU does not yet have
Strategic-autonomy / Ownership Control Declaration and EUCI/SEN handling raise the operational compliance bar
Quantum-safe homomorphic encryption is a specialised sub-field that ZNU does not currently cover; a partner with PETs / cryptography depth is needed
No documented cryptography / hardware-security lab at ZNU — risk of being scoped out of the 'Private AI' pillar without strong partners
verdict.rationale: This is the cleanest direct fit between the topic call and the AI & Automated Systems Lab's stated capabilities — adversarial robustness, anomaly detection on training data, and federated learning are all within reach for the existing AI/ML and distributed-computing teams. The 'AI in logistics systems for national security' project and Ukraine's frontline operational context together give ZNU a credible, hard-to-replicate evidence base for the real-world-adversarial-pressure angle. The honest gap is on cryptography / PETs depth (homomorphic encryption, secure aggregation, hardware-rooted trust) — these require a specialised partner from an ECCC-affiliated cybersecurity competence centre, ideally surfaced via NTNU's Norwegian or a German (BSI-linked) network. With ≈4 months of prep, the realistic ambition is Partner / WP lead in a consortium led by an experienced CL3 cybersecurity coordinator. Verdict 'yes' is conditional on lining up that coordinator within ≈6 weeks; otherwise the call risks slipping to 'maybe' as the timeline shortens.
